questionText: Consider a system with 3 processes that share 4 instances of the same resource type. Each process can request a maximum of $K$ instances. Resource instances can be requested and released only one at a time. The largest value of $K$ that will always avoid deadlock is _____.
explanation:
Given Data:
Number of processes ($N$) = $3$
Total resource instances ($R$) = $4$
Maximum demand per process = $K$

Condition to Avoid Deadlock:
For a system with $N$ processes sharing $R$ identical resources, deadlock is guaranteed to be avoided if:
$R \ge \sum_{i=1}^{N} (Demand_i - 1) + 1$

Since all $N$ processes have the maximum demand of $K$ instances:
$R \ge N \times (K - 1) + 1$

Calculation:
Substituting the values into the formula:
$4 \ge 3 \times (K - 1) + 1$
$3 \ge 3(K - 1)$
$1 \ge K - 1$
$K \le 2$

Thus, the largest value of $K$ that will always avoid deadlock is 2.
